san-may--cau-go-san-may-binh-minh: Known for a thick, rolling sea of clouds around 5:30–6:30 am. At about 1,600 m the clouds blanket the valley and the tea hills below; the best shot is the red sun rising through the clouds onto the rustic wooden bridge.
san-may--doi-da-phu: A gentle hill of green grass (rainy season) or golden grass (dry season) dotted with old pines and wide views over the valley and part of the city. At night the greenhouses of Thai Phien glow below, perfect for camping; at dawn thin mist drifts through the pines.
san-may--doi-thien-phuc-duc: Views straight to Langbiang peak in the clouds, and one of the few spots beautiful at both sunrise and a purple sunset. The hilltop is wide and breezy, with low grass ideal for an afternoon picnic.
san-may--dinh-hon-bo: At 1,709 m, Hon Bo looks down on Thai Phien flower village. It is famous for light rays piercing the morning fog, the Milky Way on clear nights, and the feeling of standing above rolling clouds.
san-may--dinh-pinhatt: Where Langbiang shows the city, Pinhatt shows wild highland nature: Tuyen Lam Lake with its islands, Truc Lam Monastery and the Robin Hill cable car below. The climb is a fun forest trek past wild orchids and ancient ferns.
san-may--khu-du-lich-dinh-langbiang: Two parts: Radar Peak (1,929 m, reached by jeep) and Ba Peak for trekking. From the top you see Suoi Vang and Suoi Bac lakes, all of Da Lat and vast forests; there are photo spots, a viewpoint cafe and a thrilling old-jeep ride up.
san-may--binh-yen-house: In the Trai Mat area, a simple A-frame wooden house on the hillside surrounded by daisies or roses. Open the window at dawn and the sea of clouds is right there; the vintage, rustic space is made for reading and hot tea.
san-may--tiem-ca-phe-binh-minh-oi: On Hoang Hoa Tham with an open valley view, an easy sunrise and cloud-hunting spot close to the centre. Known for its white daisy garden, classic wooden house and acoustic sets early morning and evening.
san-may--thien-duong-san-may-cau-dat: Part of the Cau Dat tea hills about 25 km from the centre, this is one of Da Lat's best-known cloud-hunting parks, a well-planned complex above 1,600 m built for the perfect sea-of-clouds view.
cafe-rung-thong--tiem-ca-phe-tui-mo-to: A nostalgic photo favourite inside Reply1994 Homestay, with old wooden houses and tin roofs that feel like a trip back to the countryside.
cafe-rung-thong--in-the-forest: Tucked into a pine forest in a valley near Mimosa Pass, a quiet escape built mostly of wood. Highlights are a wooden balcony over the hillside and a small turquoise pond in the middle.
cafe-rung-thong--me-linh-coffee-garden: In Ta Nung, about 20 km out, one of the largest and oldest cafes around Da Lat, known for its weasel coffee farm. It has a sweeping 360° view over the hills and Cam Ly reservoir, in a fully open, breezy space.
cafe-rung-thong--the-wilder-nest: Peaceful and a little wistful, great for bohemian or dreamy photo shoots, with the wind whistling over the grassy hill.
cafe-rung-thong--lululola-coffee: At the top of Prenn Pass, the pioneer of 'music among the clouds' in Da Lat, combining coffee, food and high-quality live acoustic shows.
cafe-rung-thong--khu-vuon-mua-he: On Dang Thai Than slope, a garden cafe like a page from a Western fairy tale, focused on lush, carefully tended plants rather than a big valley view.
cafe-rung-thong--horizon-coffee: At the top of Prenn Pass, once a social media hit as the 'garden above the clouds', with a hilltop location and one-of-a-kind architecture.
cafe-mong-mo--cay-cam-ngot: Sweet and gentle, inspired by the book 'My Sweet Orange Tree', with warm wooden tones, a small pebbled yard and sunny wooden windows.
cafe-mong-mo--ngoi-nha-la-phong: Inside the La Phong tourist area, Kokoro is a little Japan: Zen, minimalist wooden architecture in harmony with nature.
cafe-mong-mo--la-mappa-cafe-aventura: A garden villa mixing South American and classic European style on quiet Trieu Viet Vuong street, calm and discreet like a luxury retreat.
cafe-mong-mo--the-little-cottage: Like a cottage in the English countryside: vintage, sweet pastel tones and flowers all around the house.
cafe-mong-mo--nhat-nang: A simple retro cafe full of nostalgia on a high slope that catches the sun, with daisies and greenery. Sipping hot tea on the balcony over the quiet town is the draw.
cafe-mong-mo--linh-lam: Wrapped in greenery with a fully open space and plenty of fresh air, a quiet corner to unwind with only wind and rustling leaves.
cafe-mong-mo--khu-vuon-mua-he: Lush and green with hundreds of plants and ferns, cottagecore style, rustic but refined. Sunlight through the leaves makes it a haven for dreamy photo shoots.
cafe-mong-mo--chip-s-corner: A cute little corner true to its name, young and modern with a Korean touch.
cafe-mong-mo--nha-hoa-la: An open space among potted plants and climbing flowers, with furniture mostly of recycled wood and bamboo.
cafe-mong-mo--do-do: Inspired by Do Do village in Nguyen Nhat Anh's 'Mat Biec': an old general store with wooden furniture, black-and-white TVs, typewriters and vintage decor, plus lots of cats.
cafe-cho-tre-em--dang-dan-cafe-kids-hous: One of Da Lat's best-rated indoor cafe and play centres for cleanliness and safety, modern and bright. Play zones include a giant ball pit, role-play areas (doctor, cooking, supermarket), a dress-up corner and Lego; toys are new and cleaned often.
cafe-cho-tre-em--dream-house-ca-phe-thu-: A farm and pet cafe for animal-loving kids: they can pet and take photos with corgis, golden retrievers and fluffy British cats, with a big garden to run around.
cafe-cho-tre-em--kids-coffee: Gentle outdoor play such as slides, swings, seesaws and a sandpit, so kids get fresh Da Lat air instead of sitting indoors.
cafe-cho-tre-em--khu-vui-choi-tre-em-hap: A colourful indoor playground with a big play structure, spiral slides, climbing nets, a large ball pit and trampolines, great for active kids to burn energy.
cafe-cho-tre-em--khu-vui-choi-tre-em-oh-: Korean pastel style with an educational focus: besides active play there are workshops like statue painting, drawing and sand art, a reading corner and wooden Montessori toys.
cafe-cho-tre-em--horizon-kids-coffee: A large, well-equipped play centre with plenty of room and areas split by age: active zones for older kids and gentle play for toddlers.
thac-nuoc--thac-pongour-thac-bay-tang: Called the finest waterfall of the South and one of Lam Dong's grandest. Water flows over seven wide, flat rock tiers, forming beautiful white sheets.
thac-nuoc--thac-voi-lieng-rowoa: Wild and powerful: water drops 30 m onto black rocks shaped like crouching elephants. The mossy stone steps down are slippery and hard for older people and young children; combine it with the giant Guan Yin statue at Linh An Pagoda next door.
thac-nuoc--thac-datanla: Da Lat's most developed waterfall park, with steady water all year. Famous for the longest alpine coaster in Southeast Asia through the pines and for canyoning (abseiling and sliding down falls).
thac-nuoc--thac-prenn: Reopened with a new look after a long renovation; the fall is still gentle, like a thin curtain of water.
thac-nuoc--thac-cam-ly: A low, gentle waterfall over granite rocks, famous in poetry and history and linked to Dr Yersin.
thac-nuoc--thac-bao-dai-jraiblian: A wild, little-known fall hidden in the Ta In forest, said to be where King Bao Dai came to hunt and rest. Tall and quiet, but with almost no services and a steep, lonely path down; for those who love untouched nature.
thac-nuoc--thac-ankroet-tuyet-tinh-coc: Site of Vietnam's first hydropower plant. The water flows from Suoi Vang Lake into an emerald pool at the foot, nicknamed 'Tuyet Tinh Coc' by young people.
thac-nuoc--thac-bobla-thac-lien-dam: A tall fall plunging straight down like white silk in the old forest; the Bobla park has been nicely upgraded.
ho-nuoc--ho-xuan-huong: The 'heart of Da Lat', a crescent lake almost 7 km around, ringed by grass, pines and cherry blossoms in spring, and the city's main gathering place.
ho-nuoc--ho-tuyen-lam: Da Lat's largest freshwater lake (320 ha) and a national tourist area, surrounded by vast three-needle pine forest, green and peaceful.
ho-nuoc--ho-than-tho: Linked to the tragic love legend of the 'Hill of Two Graves' (Tam and Thao), a quiet, melancholy lake reflecting old pines.
ho-nuoc--ho-suoi-vang: The lake that supplies Da Lat's drinking water: wild, grand and much larger than the other lakes.
ho-nuoc--ho-da-thien: The heart of the Valley of Love park, formed by damming the Da Thien stream and surrounded by pine hills and well-kept flower gardens.
biet-thu-co--dinh-i-king-palace: Called the most beautiful of King Bao Dai's palaces after a careful restoration, on a 1,550 m hill surrounded by old pines.
biet-thu-co--dinh-ii-dinh-toan-quyen: Former residence of Indochina Governor-General Jean Decoux, built like a fortress with distinctive yellow-brown washed stone.
biet-thu-co--dinh-iii-biet-dien-bao-dai: The official home and office of King Bao Dai's family in Da Lat, the best preserved of the three palaces.
biet-thu-co--cung-nam-phuong-hoang-hau: Actually the villa of Nguyen Huu Hao, given to his daughter Queen Nam Phuong; a solid classic French building on a high hill.
biet-thu-co--biet-dien-tran-le-xuan: Former retreat of Madame Tran Le Xuan's family, now National Archives Centre IV, home of the Nguyen dynasty woodblocks (UNESCO Memory of the World) used to print books in Han-Nom script.
biet-thu-co--khu-biet-thu-cadasa: Over ten old French villas hidden under pines on one of Da Lat's prettiest roads, now mainly a high-end resort; visitors can stop at its restaurant or cafe.
biet-thu-co--lang-biet-thu-ana-mandara: A five-star resort that preserves a 1920s French village, the one place in Da Lat that feels like living in rural France.
biet-thu-co--biet-thu-hang-nga-crazy-hou: One of the world's most unusual buildings, by architect Dang Viet Nga: no rules, just shapes like ancient tree trunks, caves and giant spider webs.
vuon-hoa--the-florest-hoa-trong-rung: Currently Da Lat's largest and most popular flower garden, reached by a lovely pine-lined road. Fields of hydrangea, heather and snowball flowers, natural and wild with few concrete props.
vuon-hoa--canh-dong-hoa-cam-tu-cau-trai-: A classic photo spot for Da Lat's signature flower, with big hydrangeas all year. The highlight is a Da Lat version of the Golden Bridge held by giant hands.
vuon-hoa--fresh-garden-da-lat: In Van Thanh flower village, a colourful flower park with many models; clean paths, plenty of rest stops and easy photos make it good for families with kids or older people.
vuon-hoa--vuon-hoa-thanh-pho: A long-standing city symbol with hundreds of rare flowers and the venue of the yearly Flower Festival: roses, orchids, cacti, hydrangeas and more. Classic and traditional, better for a stroll than trendy photos.
vuon-hoa--lang-hoa-van-thanh: Da Lat's largest and oldest flower village, supplying roses to the whole country. Growers open their greenhouses so you can see roses, gerberas and lilies being grown.
vuon-hoa--vuon-thuong-uyen-bay: A lavish park in European royal style, very colourful, with Vietnam's longest rose path, a colourful sky gate and elaborately trimmed gardens.
vuon-hoa--thung-lung-hoa-ta-nung: Big seasonal fields of cosmos, buckwheat or yellow mustard flowers with views over the coffee valley and a cafe to rest; a good stop on the Ta Nung pass road.
vuon-hoa--lang-hoa-thai-phien: Da Lat's biggest chrysanthemum village. By day it is rows of greenhouses; at night thousands of lights warm the flowers and the whole valley glows.
ngam-hoang-hon--ho-tuyen-lam: One of Da Lat's best free sunset spots; the dam or boat pier gives the best angle as the still lake mirrors the orange sky between dark pines.
ngam-hoang-hon--tiem-ca-phe-tui-mo-to: Ideal for the moment day turns to night: the sun sets behind Langbiang and the greenhouse lights in the valley switch on, with the daisy garden glowing in the late light.
ngam-hoang-hon--doi-thien-phuc-duc: Come here for Da Lat's signature purple sunset sky; a lone pine against a red sky is the classic shot, on a wide, windy hilltop.
ngam-hoang-hon--bohem-coffee: Famous for a small wooden bridge over the valley. Sunsets here come with cocktails and lo-fi music, a relaxing pick for couples.
ngam-hoang-hon--ho-xuan-huong: No need to go far: take a bench or a swan boat out on the lake. The sky and buildings like Thuy Ta reflect on the water, changing quickly from gold to purple.
ngam-hoang-hon--tiem-ca-phe-hoang-hon-ch: An open design with mirrors to catch the light, set high with an unobstructed view of the sun sinking like a fireball into the clouds.
ngam-hoang-hon--lululola-coffee: One of the best valley sunset views at the top of Prenn Pass: watch the sky change colour right behind the stage while a singer performs live.
ngam-hoang-hon--doi-da-phu: Watch the whole city light up from the hilltop. Young people often pitch tents and light campfires here to wait for the sunset.
ngam-hoang-hon--doi-thong-tin: Not yet touristy, with a very open view; good for groups who want privacy and a picnic at sunset without crowds.
ngam-hoang-hon--cafe-chuyen-cua-nang: Lots of glass and wood to catch the light, a cosy sunset view over green farm hills, great for backlit photos.
ngam-hoang-hon--tram-ky-uc: Part of a photo-spot complex, with old brick walls and a distant valley view; an easy, uncrowded sunset stop.
ngam-hoang-hon--xom-leo: Da Lat's liveliest sunset spot: an embankment lined with street food carts. Sit on plastic stools with grilled rice paper and soy milk as the sun sets over the greenhouses.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-sach-hiep-luc: One of the first farms using high hydroponic racks in Da Lat. Mostly New Zealand and French berries, big and sweet; very clean, with fruit at hand height so no bending.
vuon-dau-tay--puppy-farm-nong-trai-cun: A popular 3-in-1: pets, flowers and strawberries. After playing with the dogs, visitors pick ripe Japanese and Korean berries in a large high-tech garden.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-biofresh: Inside the Than Tho Lake area, grown to European standards in greenhouses without pesticides. Known for mulberries and fragrant, crisp French strawberries.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-thang-thinh: The 'strawberry farm above the clouds' in Lac Duong, with huge greenhouses and Israeli irrigation. Its American Albion berries are firm and travel well.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-chu-hung: A well-known old farm on the Thanh Mau strawberry road; the friendly owner loves explaining his methods, with both soil beds and raised racks.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-tung-nguyen: A high-tech organic farm, mostly New Zealand berries: deep red, solid and very sweet, safe to pick and eat on the spot.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-nhat-bfarm: Specialises in Japanese varieties like Sky Berry and white 'Snow White' strawberries, a rare treat, in a neat, stylish garden.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-88: One of few farms still growing in traditional soil rows, showing old-style Da Lat strawberry farming, with lower prices and rich flavour.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-my: A large American-style farm on the road to Suoi Vang, with big, firm, sweet-and-sour berries in an open, airy setting.
vuon-dau-tay--vuon-dau-cuc-hoa-mi: Strawberries alongside rows of white daisies, the most photogenic farm on the list: pick berries and take photos among the flowers.
nha-tho--nha-tho-chanh-toa-nha-tho-con-g: Da Lat's largest church, right in the centre, one of the city's most iconic and oldest French-built landmarks.
nha-tho--nha-tho-mai-anh-domaine-de-mari: The pink church on a hill full of cherry blossoms, a modernised take on classic European church architecture.
nha-tho--nha-tho-giao-xu-cam-ly: One of Da Lat's first churches built for the local ethnic people, its roof styled after the traditional Rong communal house blended with Western design.
nha-tho--nha-tho-giao-xu-du-sinh: Da Lat's only church built in East Asian style, with curved roofs and ornaments familiar to locals and intriguing to foreign visitors.
nha-tho--hoc-vien-don-bosco-da-lat: An old, solemn building in European style, surrounded by pines, mimosa, cherry blossoms and hydrangeas, like a little Europe in the hills.
nha-tho--hoi-thanh-tin-lanh: A peaceful Protestant church with simple yet charming architecture.
nha-tho--nha-tho-thanh-mau: A 1,200 m² church in classic Western style on a high hill, lit up with lights every evening.
nha-tho--nha-tho-tung-lam: A simple, modern European-style church on a hill, less ornate than the older buildings.
nha-tho--nha-tho-thanh-tam: A church near the centre in classic European style, shaded by trees, a quiet spot amid the busy town.
nha-tho--nha-tho-giao-xu-vinh-son: A new, modern church with a spacious interior and many stained-glass windows that create beautiful light.
camping--lon-ton-camp-art: See the sea of clouds, sunrise and sunset right from your tent.
camping--doi-da-phu: 5 km from the centre, good for cloud hunting.
camping--cay-thong-co-don: A lake view, perfect for sunsets, with plenty of open space.
camping--the-campville-da-lat: Greenhouse views, sunsets and cloud hunting, with frequent deals.
camping--dalat-camp: Next to fields of seasonal flowers.
camping--lux-camp-da-lat: Paddle a SUP to the campsite; tents are pre-pitched with tables and chairs out front.
camping--doi-thien-phuc-duc: Close to the centre, with pines, pink grass and city views.
camping--twin-beans-farm: Peaceful, with a stream in front of the tents and a small bar.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-le-van: Naturally wind-dried persimmons with no heat or chemicals. The friendly owner welcomes visitors all year and lets you pick fruit; only 3 km (10 minutes) from the centre.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-trai-thai-long: A trusted garden with a friendly owner; pick persimmons yourself and choose from hundreds of photo spots.
vuon-hong-trai--moc-tra-farm: Free entry; have a coffee with a view of the wind turbines. Their dried persimmons use only top-quality fruit, often with promotions.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-da-lat-ba-tai: Near primary forest, with fresh air and a babbling stream. The trees are low so you can pick fruit without climbing.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-doc-tinh: One of Da Lat's top persimmon gardens, trusted for quality and fair prices. Sells fresh and dried persimmons and other specialties, mostly the local egg-shaped variety.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-ong-thang: A well-known garden just 10 minutes from the centre, free to visit, with modern packaging and fair prices.
vuon-hong-trai--vuon-hong-chan-deo-mimos: Low trees close to the ground so you can just reach out and pick; good for outings with friends and family.
vuon-hong-trai--tiem-ca-phe-tui-mo-to: A famous cafe with bright red persimmon trees perfect for photos; in season, strings of drying persimmons hang in the wooden house.
check-in-vintage--ga-da-lat: Vietnam's oldest railway station, 3 km from the centre, in Indochine style with curved roofs echoing Langbiang mountain.
check-in-vintage--goc-hong-kong-cho-da-l: From the small bridge linking Hoa Binh area to the market, a corner that looks like 1980s Hong Kong: peeling white paint, rusty railings and old yellow bulbs.
check-in-vintage--vien-nghien-cuu-khoa-h: A Gothic-style stone building with many windows, like a Western castle; its old mossy stones make it feel like Europe.
check-in-vintage--biet-dien-tran-le-xuan: Over 13,000 m² with three villas, each in its own aristocratic style. The blue-tiled pool has become a favourite photo spot.
check-in-vintage--nguyet-vong-lau: In the city centre, a striking red building in classic East Asian style that looks dreamy in the Da Lat mist.
check-in-vintage--dinh-i-bao-dai: Called the most beautiful of Bao Dai's palaces after restoration. A pleasant walk up, with hundreds of flowers, a rainbow staircase and a European fountain for photos.
check-in-vintage--ana-mandara-villas-dal: A resort of classic French architecture in a pine forest, featured in music videos by Erik, Minh Hang and Orange, with programmes open to visitors.
check-in-vintage--cho-da-lat: Da Lat's historic market selling produce, food and clothes, also a top photo spot, especially the Hong Kong corner beside it and around Tet.
check-in-vintage--khu-hoa-binh: Simple, nostalgic photos in the heart of the city: small cafes, the old cinema front and the streets around.
check-in-vintage--quan-van: A vintage cafe decorated like old Da Lat, cool and peaceful.
du-lich-sinh-thai--the-florest-hoa-trong: A giant flower garden in a valley ringed by primary pine forest in Ta Nung: tens of hectares, a film-like forest road and seasonal flower fields, perfect for nature photo shoots.
du-lich-sinh-thai--mongo-land-tieu-mong-: A lively outdoor fun park with colourful nomad tents, dry tubing, grass sliding and animals (alpacas, sheep, rabbits), facing a green valley; great for families and team building.
du-lich-sinh-thai--hoang-long-ohayo: An eco park in Japanese style with sculpted bonsai gardens, koi ponds and stone paths, a calm Zen space blending local plants and design.
du-lich-sinh-thai--samten-hills-dalat: A vast spiritual and eco site home to the world's largest prayer wheel in gold-plated copper, on high hills overlooking the Don Duong valley, in Vajrayana Buddhist style.
du-lich-sinh-thai--kdl-sinh-thai-cao-ngu: Halfway up Ta Nung pass, a living botanical park with thousands of flowers, forest paths, an infinity pool facing pines and an open cafe; ideal for sunsets.
du-lich-sinh-thai--nong-trai-cun-puppy-f: A hugely popular farm tourism spot with pets: bright hydrangea gardens, high-rack hydroponic strawberries and succulents, plus cute dogs to play with in a green farm setting, relaxing for adults and kids alike.
du-lich-sinh-thai--khu-du-lich-thuy-thua: Once Southeast Asia's largest coffee factory, now a large eco park with viral photo spots. Wooden decks stretch over the valley so you can sip coffee while clouds drift over old pines.
du-lich-sinh-thai--the-campville-da-lat: A glamping site among flower fields facing the Xuan Tho 'valley of lights', with stylish white tents, full amenities and outdoor BBQ; watch sunrise and clouds from your bed, far from the city noise.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--xq-da-lat-su-quan: A traditional 'village' of wooden architecture and quiet gardens celebrating Vietnam's master hand embroidery, with exquisite works like living paintings and a glimpse into the artisans' lives.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--vien-nghien-cuu-kho: In an old French Gothic stone building (a former Redemptorist monastery), holding thousands of specimens of Central Highlands flora and fauna; its mossy stone corridors suit nostalgic, cinematic photos.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--bao-tang-lam-dong: On a high hill, the museum preserves Lam Dong's history and the cultures of the Ma, K'Ho and Churu peoples. The highlight is Queen Nam Phuong's palace, with mementos of Vietnam's last queen.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--bao-tang-tra-long-d: Lam Dong's first museum dedicated to tea, telling the story of tea culture, Oolong processing and Cau Dat's tea history, in refined modern architecture with views over the tea hills.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--pho-ben-doi-creativ: A contemporary creative space connecting artists, architects and art lovers, with frequent exhibitions, workshops and projects inspired by Da Lat.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--duong-ham-dieu-khac: An elaborate tunnel sculpted entirely from red basalt clay, retelling Da Lat's history through giant sculptures of the railway station, the Chicken Church, Xuan Huong Lake and more.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--le-lycee-art-space-: Inside the Ana Mandara resort, an art space in a converted old French high school (Lycee Yersin), showing fine paintings and sculpture in romantic Indochine architecture.
bao-tang-nghe-thuat--biet-thu-hang-nga-c: A surreal work by architect Dang Viet Nga, shaped like giant tree roots and strange natural forms, like stepping into Alice in Wonderland; one of the world's boldest buildings.
farm-thu--nong-trai-cun-puppy-farm: A favourite with young people and families, famous for its friendly dogs, from corgis, huskies and malamutes to gentle golden retrievers, always ready to play.
farm-thu--mongo-land: A mini Mongolian steppe in the Ta Nung valley with colourful nomad tents and green lawns: dress up as a nomad, try grass sliding and meet alpacas, sheep and rabbits.
farm-thu--zoodoo-zoo-vuon-thu-zoodoo: Run like an Australian-style friendly zoo: animals live semi-wild under the pines rather than in cages. Keepers introduce you to kangaroos, alpacas, ponies and fluffy sheep, and you can feed them yourself.
farm-thu--the-bunny-hill: A peaceful, cute spot home to hundreds of rabbits of many breeds, with camping and garden coffee; quieter than the big farms.
farm-thu--doi-thu-kim-ngan-da-lat: A large hilltop farm in Xuan Tho with ostriches, sheep, goats and colourful birds, open views over a green valley and plenty of room for kids to run.
lang-nghe--lang-hoa-van-thanh: Da Lat's oldest and best-known flower village, now a high-tech farm tourism hub famous for roses, strawberries, black tomatoes and pepino melons grown hydroponically.
lang-nghe--lang-hoa-thai-phien: One of the biggest growing areas, supplying chrysanthemums and lilies nationwide, and the source of Da Lat's legendary 'valley of lights' when thousands of greenhouse lamps glow at night.
lang-nghe--lang-hoa-ha-dong: Da Lat's first flower village, founded in 1938 by migrants from Ha Tay, with Northern-style houses and gardens and classic, traditional flowers.
lang-nghe--lang-det-tho-cam-xa-lat-buon-: At the foot of Langbiang, a centre of K'Ho culture where you can watch artisans hand-weave intricate brocade.
lang-nghe--lang-che-cau-dat-so-tra-cau-d: A 100-year-old heritage from the French era and one of Southeast Asia's oldest working tea factories. Green tea hills roll to the horizon beside giant wind turbines, and the old machinery is a living museum.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--wonderland-dalat-wo: Inside Dalat Wonder Resort on Tuyen Lam Lake, a European-style mini amusement park: a -4°C snow house, a friendly zoo, a hill coaster and VR games.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--puppy-farm-nong-tra: More than a pet farm: kids play with dozens of gentle dog breeds, then explore flower gardens and high-tech plots of strawberries, cherry tomatoes and giant pumpkins.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--la-dalat: Inside Ladalat hotel, one of the city's biggest and most modern indoor play centres, with active play, role-play, brain games and video games; great on rainy or cold days.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--vuon-thu-zoodoo: About 40 km from the centre, an Australian-style zoo where keepers guide kids to meet alpacas, kangaroos, ponies and sheep and feed them in a natural setting.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--dalat-fairytale-lan: Inspired by fairy tales and the Hobbit village: tiny houses under trees, a mysterious wine cellar and winding trails that spark children's imagination; great for family photos.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--mongo-land: A slice of the Mongolian steppe on the outskirts: grass sliding, Mongolian tents and rabbits, sheep and goats on wide lawns, with a relaxing green valley view for parents.
khu-vui-choi-tre-em--thung-lung-tinh-yeu: A legendary Da Lat park with plenty for kids: a wax museum, swan boats on Da Thien Lake, a giant hedge maze and games in the flower park.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--green-box-coffee-far: A modern cafe and mini farm museum: sip fresh juice while walking among hydroponic greens in the greenhouse, learning about farm-to-table in a hands-on way.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--puppy-farm: Beyond the dogs, Puppy Farm's high-tech section grows colourful coffee cherries, giant pumpkins and strawberries hydroponically, perfect for bright farm photos.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--vuon-rau-biofresh: A pioneer of French technology in Da Lat farming, specialising in strawberries and specialty vegetables grown hydroponically under strict control.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--vuon-bi-ngo-dau-tay-: Famous for pumpkins weighing tens to hundreds of kilos and rows of sweet red Japanese strawberries of perfectly even size.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--da-lat-gap: A symbol of clean food in Vietnam: a showroom and display garden of GlobalGAP-certified vegetables grown in closed hydroponic systems; very educational.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--lang-nam-da-lat: A magical world of mushrooms grown organically and with high tech: see how they are cared for, taste mushroom soup on site and learn about rare species.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--vuon-dua-pepino-dinh: The place to discover pepino, a golden melon tasting like a mix of cantaloupe and pear, heavy on the vines, alongside tree tomatoes and unusual vegetables.
vuon-rau-thuy-canh--vuon-dau-rau-hiep-lu: Known for strawberries on high racks and multi-level hydroponic greens, with clean, dry paths; giant tomatoes and crisp lettuce make popular take-home gifts.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--doi-robin-cap-t: At the southern gateway of the city, the start of the 2 km cable car to Truc Lam Monastery, with views over pine forests, misty valleys, Prenn Pass and Tuyen Lam Lake.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--dinh-langbiang-: The 'roof of Da Lat' at nearly 2,000 m with a 360° view. After a jeep ride up, see Suoi Vang and Suoi Bac shimmering and Lac Duong among the clouds.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--dalat-nights-ca: At the top of Prenn Pass, the classic spot to see Da Lat sparkle at night; glass walls let you sip something warm while the city lights spill into the valley.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--khu-da-chien-ch: A cluster of rustic wooden cafes on a hillside facing the Nam Ho valley, famous for superb sunsets and the greenhouse lights coming on at dusk.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--dinh-pinhatt: The highest peak south of the city, with a wild, unique view over Tuyen Lam Lake after an easy trek through the pines.
ngam-da-lat-tu-tren-cao--doi-thien-phuc-: Facing Langbiang, known for its 'lonely tree' and brilliant cloud-hunting mornings, with white clouds filling the valley; a quiet, wild spot for a pure sunrise.
cheo-kayak-sup--tour-san-suong-may-binh-: The best activity for early risers: paddle Tuyen Lam Lake as it wakes, as the first rays cut through the pines and turn the mist gold.
cheo-kayak-sup--tour-ngam-hoang-hon-rung: A romantic kayak trip across Tuyen Lam Lake into a maple forest, rare in Vietnam, with red and gold leaves late in the year and a sunset over the water.
cong-troi--cong-troi-bali-green-hills: Near Robin Hill, a recreation of Bali's Lempuyang temple gate; a mirror creates perfect symmetrical photos against the blue sky and pines.
cong-troi--da-lat-view-cong-troi-nhat: Bright red Japanese torii gates atop Mimosa Pass with views over pine forest and deep valley, great for Kimono or period-style photos.
cong-troi--cong-troi-me-linh-me-linh-cof: Part of the famous 360° view cafe in Ta Nung, the gate faces vast coffee fields and a clear lake, a free and open spot to breathe fresh highland air.
cong-troi--thien-duong-san-may-cau-dat: A gateway to the morning sea of clouds on the 100-year-old Cau Dat tea hills, with a wooden bridge and wind turbines appearing through the clouds.
cong-troi--vuon-thuong-uyen-bay: Like a royal garden floating in the clouds, with an ornate sky gate and colourful flower paths, a dreamy spot for lovers of temperate flowers.
cong-troi--linh-quy-phap-an-bao-loc: In Bao Loc, about 120 km from Da Lat, the original and most meaningful 'sky gate' on the list: meditation gates at a pagoda with absolute serenity, especially at sunrise or sunset in the mist.
bar-pub--the-balcony-speakeasy-bar: A true hidden speakeasy with a surprising entrance and a balcony over quiet Quang Trung street; classy and classic, perfect for a Negroni or Old Fashioned.
bar-pub--on-the-rocks: In a basement, mysterious and artistic, with skilled mixologists who make off-menu cocktails to match your mood; cosy and dimly lit for long talks.
bar-pub--woody-classic-bar: Warm wood all around in a classic European pub style, one of Da Lat's earliest bars and still consistently good, with a huge list from fine whisky to cocktails with local ingredients.
bar-pub--fox-s-den-hang-cao: Small, warm and cut off from the noise like a real fox's den, with quiet music; great for going solo or with a close friend.
bar-pub--gemination-eatery-bar-da-lat: Fine dining meets cocktail craft in a stylish contemporary space: start with dinner and finish with signature cocktails.
bar-pub--b21bar: Lively and young, a hangout for young people and foreign travellers with catchy music and an open space; the place to let off steam.
bar-pub--hem-ky-uc-memory-lane-bar-coffe: In a quiet alley, coffee by day and cocktails by night, with gentle nostalgic decor; sip a gin and tonic to romantic indie tunes.
bar-pub--the-classic-pub-nguyet-vong-lau: On the famous corner of the red Nguyet Vong Lau house, one of Da Lat's most iconic photo spots, keeping its red walls and old windows.
bar-pub--don-quixote: Inspired by the dreamy knight, artsy and free-spirited, rustic with honest Da Lat service and simple, good drinks.
show-nhac--may-lang-thang: One of Da Lat's most iconic outdoor music venues, on a hill overlooking the misty valley, famous for sunset shows with top artists.
show-nhac--lululola: At the city gateway, overlooking pine valleys and Prenn Pass, known for live shows starting at dusk in an open, refined space.
show-nhac--phong-tra-cung-dan-xua: A music lounge in an old French villa in the centre, focused on pre-war songs, Trinh Cong Son and timeless love songs; elegant, cosy and nostalgic.
show-nhac--may-in-the-nest: A special stage tucked in the pine forest of Mang Lin, where music blends with untouched nature, far from the city.
cafe-acoustic--sense-cafe-acoustic: A fresh, modern take on acoustic music, with a quality sound system and a close connection between artists and audience.
cafe-acoustic--can-nha-xua-guitar-moc: Classic wooden architecture and dim yellow lights; here it's all unplugged, just acoustic guitar and voice, with old love songs and timeless foreign hits.
cafe-acoustic--quan-cafe-nhac-trinh-acou: An elegant art space on Hung Vuong street dedicated to Trinh Cong Son, Ngo Thuy Mien and classic love songs, with piano and violin.
cafe-acoustic--tiem-ca-phe-binh-minh-oi: Known for acoustic nights among the pines, with mist drifting right by your seat and greenhouse lights twinkling in the distance.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--dalat-camp: A glamping icon deep in a secluded valley in Da Sar, with golf-course-like lawns and a European-style wooden lodge; no Wi-Fi, so you truly disconnect.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--twin-beans-farm: A coffee farm with camping: white bell tents by a stream and Arabica fields. Join coffee picking, hand roasting and stream bathing like a real highland farmer.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--la-an-retreat: A secluded retreat in wild Suoi Can with wide lawns, a still lake and a small stream, built with natural wood and stone; ideal for creative workshops or finding balance.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--lang-cu-lan: An eco park at the foot of Langbiang rich in K'Ho culture, with stilt houses, pine forest and a winding stream; its streamside lawns are popular for camping.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--tiem-ca-phe-nha-: Famous for coffee in the middle of a stream: wooden chairs sit in shallow, cool water under the trees, a perfect way to cool off on sunny days.
cam-trai-cafe-ben-suoi--suoi-binh-yen: Hidden among bright hydrangea fields, a minimalist cafe with the sound of a natural stream, for those seeking real peace.
vibe-nhat-ban--que-garden: Near Van Thanh village, one of Vietnam's largest Japanese bonsai gardens, with hundreds of sculpted trees and a big koi pond; stroll in a Zen space and enjoy tea.
vibe-nhat-ban--kdl-la-phong-kokoro-cafe: In the La Phong park, Japanese architecture meets over 2,000 maple trees and koi ponds, especially striking when the leaves change colour.
vibe-nhat-ban--kokoro-cafe: Minimalist design, wooden floors and a fully open space to breathe the fresh air of the pine valley; a peaceful spot to slow down.
vibe-nhat-ban--still-cafe: A 'little street' of shops like a Totoro bakery, ramen shop and Ghibli-style tea house, with noren curtains and paper lanterns recreating old Kyoto.
vibe-nhat-ban--thi-tran-nobi-homestay: A faithful recreation of Doraemon's neighbourhood, from Nobita's attic room to the lot with three concrete pipes; a cafe and homestay that takes you back to childhood.
vibe-nhat-ban--da-lat-view: Known for a winding red bridge and Shinto-style gates atop Mimosa Pass with unlimited views; the red against the green forest makes striking photos.
vibe-nhat-ban--tiem-ca-phe-phia-tay-mat-: Contemporary Japanese minimalism focused on light and view, on a hillside ideal for watching the sun set west over the valley.
vibe-han-quoc--yooberi-studio-cafe: A studio cafe in modern Seoul style with sweet pastels like a Korean youth drama, with a mini store, flower shop and picnic corner; drinks are mostly cute imported cans.
vibe-han-quoc--blue-dream-bread: A handmade bakery in a cosy wooden cafe reminiscent of Samcheong-dong, with the smell of fresh bread and carefully made croissants and sourdough.
vibe-han-quoc--the-married-beans-showroo: In an old villa redone in minimalist style, with high ceilings and cool grey-white tones, showcasing Da Lat specialty coffee with professional brewing.
vibe-han-quoc--reply-1994-dalat: Inspired by the famous drama, a 1990s Korean setting with vintage decor and the misty valley around, a blend of K-retro and Da Lat soul.
vibe-han-quoc--la-lapine-bakery-coffee: A clean and chic branch on a busy street, full of natural light with big windows, serving French-standard pastries styled with modern Korean flair.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-tao-ngo-goc: The original that started Da Lat's chicken hotpot craze, at the top of Prenn Pass and always busy. Its broth is the benchmark: sweet chicken bone, green chilli heat and fragrant e leaves.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-668: A strong rival to Tao Ngo, known for carefully chosen chicken with golden skin and sweet meat and a roomier space; also try the clay-oven roast chicken.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-39-quan-lau-ngo: On Le Dai Hanh slope in the centre, handy near the Hoa Binh area, with a rich broth for strong palates and generous sour bamboo shoots and mushrooms.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-tao-ngo-89: The same Tao Ngo recipe in a more open space, with a consistently good broth.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-thuy-hieu: A distinctly spicy broth with always-fresh e leaves and simple, homely service.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-tao-ngo-hai-thu: The familiar Tao Ngo flavour in a cosy space, good for relaxed family meals.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-tao-ngo-30-phan: A fairly large branch with professional, quick service and a light, not greasy broth.
lau-ga-la-e--lau-ga-la-e-tao-ngo-dalat: Very attentive service and a clean space, with a balanced flavour that suits diners from all regions.
lau-bo--lau-bo-quan-go: The original and best-known of the Ba Toa beef hotpot area, in an old wooden house that is busy from opening. Deep beef bone broth, thick slices, tender brisket and tendon, with fermented tofu and chilli dip.
lau-bo--lau-bo-ba-toa-since-1996: Keeps the traditional Ba Toa beef hotpot flavour from the 1990s, with a light broth focused on fresh beef and Da Lat greens.
lau-bo--lau-bo-ba-toa-bi-map: Friendly service and a herb-scented broth with well-prepared beef; popular with young groups for its quick service.
lau-bo--lau-bo-ba-toa-to-bo-quan: Generous portions at fair prices, with big beef slices, chewy brisket and a rich broth that gets sweeter as it cooks.
lau-bo--lau-bo-26: A homely, rustic spot many locals prefer to avoid the big crowds, with simple flavours and very fresh ingredients.
lau-bo--lau-bo-phan-rang-da-lat: Brings a Phan Rang touch to the highlands, with a lighter broth and a Ninh Thuan-style dipping sauce.
lau-bo--lau-bo-din: Calm and elegant, focused on a clear broth and the best cuts like shank and tail; good for unhurried meals.
lau-bo--bo-to-ong-minh: Specialises in young veal: tender, sweet and milky. Besides hotpot, try grilled veal and steamed veal rolled in rice paper.
lau-bo--lau-bo-dai-phat: A trusted local favourite for consistent quality and hygiene, with a naturally sweet broth from bones and vegetables and fresh greens.
banh-can--banh-can-nha-gao: Evenly cooked cakes, lightly crisp outside and soft inside, with many toppings like egg, quail egg and minced beef, and a rich meatball dipping sauce.
banh-can--banh-can-co-le-batoa-1997: A veteran since the late 1990s near the historic Ba Toa bridge, with old-style banh can and rich meatball sauce with scallion oil.
banh-can--banh-can-be-hoa: Always busy thanks to steady quality and quick service, known for fresh seafood fillings (shrimp, squid), fish sauce or anchovy dip and sweet-sour shredded mango.
banh-can--yet-kieu-quan: A homely family spot on quiet Yet Kieu street; cakes are cooked over charcoal for a smoky aroma, with big handmade meatballs.
banh-can--banh-can-nha-co: In an old wooden house in the centre; eating hot banh can in a classic Da Lat wooden home is the treat.
banh-can--banh-can-banh-trang-co-hai: Skilled cooking with crispy bases and a varied menu, good for a light afternoon meal.
banh-can--banh-can-tang-bat-ho: Very convenient location, with easy-going flavours and always-warm dipping sauce that suits everyone.
banh-can--banh-can-hai-san-thuy: Specialises in fresh seafood banh can, with tender squid or sweet shrimp in the white cake.
banh-uot-long-ga--quan-banh-uot-long-ga-: Known for carefully prepared chicken offal with no smell and a nice crunch, thin warm rice sheets and ginger fish sauce.
banh-uot-long-ga--lien-banh-uot-long-ga-: The Lien brand is a byword for Da Lat chicken rice rolls: chewy sheets, firm free-range chicken and golden, rich skin.
banh-uot-long-ga--banh-uot-long-ga-thao: Famous for a perfectly balanced sweet-sour-spicy dipping sauce and generous, fresh chicken offal.
banh-uot-long-ga--banh-uot-long-ga-hang: Simple and homely, with rice sheets made continuously so they stay soft, and crispy homemade fried shallots.
banh-uot-long-ga--banh-uot-long-ga-long: Called the 'people's favourite', with chewy, sweet free-range chicken and a simple but always lively shop.
banh-uot-long-ga--banh-uot-long-ga-song-: Neatly presented bowls and fish sauce with a secret touch of ginger, garlic and chilli.
banh-uot-long-ga--banh-uot-long-ga-mat-d: A light, delicate flavour with clean chicken offal and fresh Da Lat herbs.
banh-trang-nuong--banh-trang-nuong-di-di: The 'legend' of Da Lat grilled rice paper, busy from opening until late, with over 20 toppings from classic to cheese, shredded chicken and sausage, grilled crisp but never burnt.
banh-trang-nuong--banh-trang-nuong-co-ta: Rustic, rich and traditional with generous toppings and a fiery homemade chilli sauce, perfect in cool weather.
banh-trang-nuong--hia-lee: Young and creative on the road to Bao Dai Palace III, with inventive toppings mixing Vietnamese street food and modern flavours, and a comfortable space.
banh-trang-nuong--banh-trang-nuong-chi-h: On the famous Nha Chung food street beside the Chicken Church; small but top quality, with buttery, eggy aroma and a thin, crisp base.
banh-trang-nuong--banh-trang-nuong-co-hu: A trusted spot on busy Nguyen Van Troi near the market, using fresh ingredients; moist egg and creamy cheese on an evenly crisp base.
banh-trang-nuong--banh-trang-nuong-suong: Carefully made with balanced flavours, in a calm, pleasant space away from the noise.
nem-nuong--quan-nem-nuong-co-thu: A cosy family-style shop with hand-pounded pork rolls that stay chewy and naturally sweet.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-cha-ram-bap-hoang-h: Crispy corn spring rolls with the aroma of young corn alongside rich grilled pork rolls, and a well-balanced dipping sauce.
nem-nuong--cha-ram-bap-nem-nuong-tan-lon: Very fast service and a roomy space; pork rolls are grilled continuously over hot charcoal so they arrive hot and fragrant.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-gia-truyen-ha-tot: The highlight is a golden, silky, deep-flavoured bean dipping sauce; the pork rolls are lightly charred for a slight crunch.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-ba-hung: Professional and large-scale, Ba Hung has become the benchmark for Da Lat grilled pork rolls, with consistent ingredients.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-hung-van: Generous pickles and fresh herbs in a clean, airy space, great for large groups.
nem-nuong--hanh-tam-bun-va-nem-nuong: Besides pork rolls wrapped in rice paper, known for rice vermicelli with grilled pork rolls, a lighter alternative.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-lien: Lean pork rolls with little fat for those who dislike greasy food, and crisp herbs from clean Da Lat gardens.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-dung-loc: A quiet 'secret' spot of local foodies near Cam Ly waterfall, with very affordable prices.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-phuong: Sweet, rich Central Vietnam-style pork rolls adapted to the cool climate, with dipping sauce kept warm on the stove.
nem-nuong--nem-nuong-ba-nghia: Known for crispy spring rolls and herb-marinated pork rolls, beautifully presented on bamboo trays.
oc-nhoi-thit--quan-oc-nhoi-thit-33-da-la: Stuffed snails served in hot clay pots: snail meat minced with pork paste and lemongrass for a chewy, sweet bite, with a signature ginger fish sauce.
oc-nhoi-thit--33-oc-nhoi-thit: Besides stuffed snails, known for rich beef and oxtail hotpot; the mix of meat, snail and lemongrass-ginger is memorable.
oc-nhoi-thit--quan-33-oc-nhoi-thit-hem-2: Careful preparation with fresh, well-cleaned snails; a local favourite away from the busy centre.
oc-nhoi-thit--oc-tam-33: Friendly, simple service; steaming pots of snails with spicy ginger fish sauce are perfect on misty nights.
oc-nhoi-thit--lau-bo-oc-33-ngon: Great for groups and families wanting several dishes: a deep beef bone hotpot alongside stuffed snails for a hearty dinner.
oc-nhoi-thit--oc-khanh-nhu: A bigger snail menu cooked many ways (garlic, salt-roasted, lemongrass-steamed), ideal for snail lovers.
sua-dau-nanh--quan-hoa-sua: Always busy with people sitting along the pavement; nicely balanced milks from soy and mung bean to peanut.
sua-dau-nanh--sua-dau-nanh-dung-beo: A favourite stop for locals and visitors after the night market, with very fast service and fresh, crispy pastries to go with your milk.
sua-dau-nanh--sua-co-lan: A trusted shop on busy Phan Dinh Phung known for pure, rich soy milk with a strong fresh-bean aroma, in a homely space.
sua-dau-nanh--sua-dau-nanh-co-phuong: Very cheap but as good as the central shops; soy milk with a touch of condensed milk for extra richness.
sua-dau-nanh--sua-dau-nanh-sua-hat-sen-s: Stands out for its range of nut milks, especially lotus seed and corn milk, made by hand to keep the full flavour.
sua-dau-nanh--sua-dau-nanh-hanh-sua-viet: A long-standing, neat and clean shop famous for mixing soy milk with fresh cow's milk for a rich blend.
kem-bo--kem-bo-da-lat-kem-bo-na-ri: A favourite for proper avocado ice cream: silky, carefully chosen avocado with no fibres, topped with fragrant, not-too-sweet coconut ice cream.
kem-bo--kem-bo-thanh-thao: The legend that made avocado ice cream a Da Lat icon, always busy, with the same recipe for decades: smooth avocado, white coconut ice cream and a little durian.
kem-bo--kem-bo-thach-thao: Another good shop on Nguyen Van Troi with a more relaxed space; well balanced, not too sweet, with natural avocado creaminess.
kem-bo--kem-phung: A long-established brand that grew from a small stall in Da Lat market, known for elegant presentation and a wide menu, including excellent fruit ice creams.
kem-bo--kem-bo-che-huyen: Inside the lively Da Lat market food area: simple but tasty avocado ice cream made with freshly blended avocado.
kem-bo--ca-rem-bong-bong: Handmade, low-sugar avocado ice cream focused on natural ingredients, beautifully presented.
kem-bo--cham: Right in the centre, a modern take on avocado ice cream, famous for scooped avocado ice cream balls, in a bright avocado-yellow space.
kem-bo--cham-cafe-kem-bo-da-lat: Cham's second branch near Da Lat station, roomier and well decorated, with the same premium avocado ice cream and a wide drinks menu.
nuong-ngoi--quan-nuong-ngoi-cu-tay: One of the oldest and best-known tile-grilling spots: big, lively and casual, with pork, beef and seafood in its own rich marinades.
nuong-ngoi--quan-ngoi-nuong: On quieter Thien My street, cosier and more private, with carefully chosen meat and refined marinades and warm service.
nuong-ngoi--nuong-ngoi-71: Top pick for convenience and modern service, with good ventilation, a clean space and a central location near the night market.
quan-nuong--khoi-lau-nuong: An open space for cosy evenings, combining richly marinated grills with hot hotpots to chase away the cold.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-tram-dung-chill: A relaxing garden-style stop where you can enjoy grilled meat to soft music, away from the city noise.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-u-nu: Known for very generous portions, fresh meat and a sweet house dipping sauce, popular with young people.
quan-nuong--matchandeul-da-lat: Upscale Korean BBQ, known for perfectly grilled fermented pork that stays juicy, in a smart space.
quan-nuong--tut-nuong: Casual and a bit rough around the edges, a go-to for groups: classic charcoal grilling at very low prices until late.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-tren-may: High on a slope, grill among the mist and watch the sunset over the whole valley.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-trong-rung: Under green pines, sit around the fire in the forest with the scent of pine resin and grilling meat.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-our-memory: Nostalgic, with warm yellow lights and a refined menu focused on quality and balanced seasoning.
quan-nuong--nam-nuong: A legend of Da Lat tile grilling: meat cooks on a red-hot clay tile so it stays juicy without burning; a must on Hoang Dieu street.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-thuong-thuong: Overlooking a deep valley, with rustic wooden tables for a gentle, romantic meal.
quan-nuong--thung-lung-den-coffee-bbq: Famous for its view over the glowing 'valley of lights' of greenhouses at night.
quan-nuong--nam-nuong-1900: A branch of Nam Nuong on Tran Phu with consistent tile- and stone-grilled dishes, professional service and an easy-to-find space.
quan-nuong--bbq-mo-te: Draws diners with a wide range of grilled seafood and game meats, right in the centre.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-mau-vang: A bright yellow theme and a large garden on Khe Sanh, great for lively outdoor BBQs with family.
quan-nuong--quan-nuong-chill-in-dalat: Modern design that makes the most of the pine valley view, with dishes on bamboo trays that are great for photos and videos.
quan-nuong--tui-nuong-lavender: Tucked in a quiet alley, private and romantic, decorated with flowers and candles.
quan-nuong--hem-chill-bbq: Another hidden alley gem, cosy and friendly with tasty grilled snacks, an escape from the big streets.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-hat-soi: On a quiet little slope, modern rustic with lots of wood, and Western-style marinades using local ingredients.
quan-nuong--quan-bo-to-ong-minh: The best-known spot for young veal, carefully chosen, tender and milky, grilled simply to let it shine.
quan-nuong--quan-nuong-lo-ghim-grill-chi: Balances grilled meat with fresh Da Lat vegetables for a healthier, less heavy BBQ.
quan-nuong--tiem-nuong-ong-thuong: Homely and warm, with simple, honest grilled dishes that feel like a BBQ in your own yard.
quan-nuong--gogi-house-da-lat: The well-known Korean BBQ chain in a central location, with consistent quality and a clean, reliable experience.
buffet--bbq-garden-da-lat-buffet-nuong-l: A varied grill buffet of beef, pork and seafood with Vietnamese marinades, and good smoke extraction despite the open space.
buffet--chill-garden-buffet: A relaxing space with a buffet of grills and hotpot and plenty of tasty side dishes.
buffet--leguda-buffet-rau-da-lat: On Robin Hill, Da Lat's most famous vegetable buffet with a 360° view over the city and Prenn Pass; dip garden-fresh greens in a split hotpot, with meat and seafood as add-ons.
buffet--buffet-nuong-khoi-bep: Simple, honest cooking over hot charcoal for that smoky flavour; a top pick for traditional grills in a quiet setting.
buffet--buffet-ba-sach: A small but quality buffet focused on fresh meat and hygiene, in a neat, polite space.
buffet--buffet-rau-robinson-da-lat: An airy restaurant focused on fresh produce, with a light, sweet broth that brings out the vegetables.
com-nieu--com-nieu-vinh-ky: One of the oldest clay pot rice restaurants, roomy and traditional, famous for its pot-smashing show, crispy rice crust and Southern-style braised fish.
com-nieu--com-nieu-viet-nam: Right next to Vinh Ky, cosy with wooden decor and a big menu of regional dishes; fresh broths and stir-fries.
com-nieu--com-nieu-vi-que: Focused on the original flavours of Da Lat produce, with impressive wild greens and mushrooms.
com-nieu--com-nieu-hoa-dao: Prime corner location, clean and professional, for those who like a neat place and slightly lighter flavours.
com-nieu--com-nieu-den-long-da-lat: Glowing with hundreds of lanterns and very warm at night, the most photogenic clay pot rice spot, good for family photos.
com-nieu--com-nieu-nhu-ngoc: A long-standing upscale brand with refined cooking and presentation in a quiet, classy setting.
